_comment: The project's optimization mandate (docs/process/optimization.md, 'Decision rights'). Copy to docs/process/optimization.local.json and set the values with the owner; without that file analysis is allowed and no trial starts. Read by scripts/process/optimize.py: `max_pilot_days` (a trial's `until` may lie at most this far ahead when it starts) and `steward_may` (rights the owner delegates: `start` a trial, `roll-back`, `reject`, `adopt`; stopping is everybody's and needs no right). The other keys are the mandate's text for whoever designs and judges a trial — goals in priority order above the floors, the floors no trial may lower, the optimization budget as a share of the measured tokens and execution time over the window, and the starting points to calibrate against the baseline. Changing this file is the owner's decision (lowering a floor, widening the steward's rights, raising a budget) and is reviewed like any process configuration. `outcomes` (read by process_kpis.py outcomes, telemetry module) says what value means here: how an epic is recognised beside native sub-issues, when it counts as usable (`epic-closed`, a proxy, or `label:<name>` / `title:<text>` naming the acceptance sub-issue), which labels mark a bug and a disruptive one, and the coverage the two bug-origin axes (cause:*, channel:*) must reach before the blind spot closes. `guardrails` (read by scripts/process/gate_modes.py) names the gates no record may weaken beside the core gates (`protected`, e.g. a security scan or a migration check) and the limits whose breach makes the sentinel restore every active weakening that touches them (`limits`: name, metric — `regressions`, commits with a `Regression-of:` trailer in the window — max, window_days). `deploy` (read by process_kpis.py flow) says whether the project has a deploy step: `false` makes the merge the endpoint by design, also for issues merged without the train; leave it out when unsure. `plan_drift` (read by scripts/process/plan_drift.py when dispatch starts an execute phase) sets that node's mode — `shadow` records only, `warn` notes it to the steward and the worker, `block` refuses the start until the plan is refreshed or `--stale-plan-ok` is passed — and the limits beyond which a plan counts as stale: `max_touching` later base commits that change a file the plan names, `max_behind` later base commits at all.
floors: no gate disabled or bypassed by a trial
no tier lowered and no review independence reduced
acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done unchanged
no change to security boundaries or data without its own Tier 3 review
